decisions.question: Will the next full gemini model be as good as opus 4.7 or gpt 5.5 at coding?
decisions.thinking: Given Gemini 3.5 Flash's strong benchmark performance, the upcoming Pro model has a high probability of matching at least GPT-5.5 or Opus 4.7 in developer hands, satisfying the 'OR' condition.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether the upcoming Gemini Pro release feels as capable in real-world developer workflows as Opus 4.7 to the market creator.
decisions.resolution_risk: The resolution relies entirely on the creator's subjective personal trial rather than an objective benchmark suite.
evidence_for: Gemini 3.5 Flash achieved 87.6% on LiveCodeBench, showing strong baseline coding capability for the generation.
The criterion requires matching EITHER Opus 4.7 OR GPT-5.5, lowering the threshold compared to needing to be the undisputed #1.
Full Pro tier models from Google historically deliver noticeable coding gains over the Flash tier.
evidence_against: Claude Opus 4.7 remains the preferred frontier choice among developers for complex, multi-file agentic coding tasks.
Creator subjective resolution means practical developer feel matters more than synthetic benchmark scores.

decisions.question: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by end of August? [Polymarket]
decisions.thinking: IMF Portwatch 7-day MA for Strait of Hormuz transits was reported around 11.1 in late July. Reaching 60+ calls/day requires a 5x jump with only 3 weeks remaining until the August 31 cutoff. Even under an immediate peace scenario, insurance and operational re-routing lag make reaching 60 by month-end highly improbable. Estimating 3% YES.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether an immediate geopolitical breakthrough occurs and shipping lines rapidly re-enter the Strait before August 31.
decisions.resolution_risk: IMF Portwatch technical data updates or retroactively revised methodology changing historical transit counts.
evidence_for: Potential rapid diplomatic de-escalation that opens the Strait to maritime traffic.
IMF Portwatch data revisions could adjust transit call counts upward.
evidence_against: IMF Portwatch data for late July shows a 7-day moving average of only ~11.1 daily transit calls, far below the 60 threshold.
Only 21 days remain before the August 31 deadline, leaving insufficient time for a 5x traffic surge.
Commercial shipping operators, maritime insurers, and logistics networks require weeks to re-route vessels even after conflict de-escalation.
